chunks: And from him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"A slave man may not possess more than two women."

key_terms.النِّسَاءِ: Women, specifically referring to female slaves or concubines in this context
key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكُ: The slave (male), referring to a male slave in the context of ownership

ai.seo_question: What is the maximum number of female slaves a man can own according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* specifies that a male slave (*abd*) is permitted to hold concubines (*riwaq*) from among other slaves, but his capacity is limited to two, distinguishing his status from that of a free man who may have up to four. This ruling highlights the nuanced hierarchy within the institution of slavery in Shia jurisprudence, where the legal capacity of a slave is restricted compared to a free person, reflecting the economic and social realities of the time. It serves as a key precedent in *fiqh al-riwaq* for determining the maximum number of concubines a slave can own simultaneously.
